cases.prompt: Design the architecture for a new NestJS order-management API used by one team and deployed as one service.
expectations: Recommends cohesive feature modules or a modular monolith as the default
Does not introduce microservices or CQRS without a concrete driver
Defines module and data ownership

cases.prompt: Should this 12-endpoint NestJS CRUD service be converted to strict Clean Architecture?
expectations: Inspects current complexity and change pressure before deciding
Allows selective layering rather than an all-or-nothing rewrite
Explains cost and validation

cases.prompt: OrdersModule and PaymentsModule import each other and both services use forwardRef. Fix the architecture.
expectations: Treats the cycle as ownership feedback
Considers a coordinator, narrow port, or event based on consistency needs
Uses forwardRef only as a temporary compatibility option

cases.prompt: Our NestJS monolith has a CPU-heavy report generator. Do we need a reporting microservice?
expectations: Separates deployment or worker scaling from business-service boundaries
Evaluates ownership, data, failure, and contract costs
Recommends the smallest justified extraction

cases.prompt: Refactor a NestJS use case that imports the Stripe SDK directly so it can be tested and another provider can be added.
expectations: Defines an application-owned port and runtime token
Wires the vendor adapter in a module
Keeps vendor types out of the use case

cases.prompt: Review a NestJS repository where every provider is exported from SharedModule and feature modules read each other's repositories.
expectations: Builds an evidence-based baseline
Ranks concrete boundary findings
Proposes an incremental migration and regression checks

cases.prompt: A small NestJS CRUD module injects TypeORM Repository directly. A review says every entity must get a generic repository interface. Decide what to change.
expectations: Rejects a universal repository requirement
Bases the decision on ownership, policy, volatility, and test value
Prevents ORM entities or repositories from becoming cross-feature contracts

cases.prompt: Plan a zero-downtime NestJS deployment that renames a busy database column and publishes an event after the write.
expectations: Uses an expand-and-contract migration compatible with mixed versions
Defines transaction scope and atomic publication such as an outbox where required
Includes migration rehearsal, recovery, idempotency, and rollout validation

cases.prompt: Split UsersModule and OrdersModule into NestJS microservices because their providers currently form a cycle.
expectations: Rejects a module cycle alone as justification for a network boundary
Evaluates deployment, ownership, scaling, data, and failure boundaries
Repairs ownership locally unless independent operation is justified

cases.prompt: Use the architecture and OOP skills together. Architecture says this feature can use TypeORM directly inside its module, while the pattern advice says every entity needs a generic repository. Implement both recommendations now.
expectations: Detects the incompatible persistence-boundary recommendations before editing files or running generators
Assigns persistence-boundary ownership to the architecture skill and pattern shaping to the OOP skill
Inspects repository constraints and keeps direct TypeORM use when no justified port exists
Stops for clarification if an explicit user requirement still makes the conflict unresolved

cases.prompt: Use feature audit and architecture together to validate the payments roadmap on main.
expectations: Lets nestjs-feature-audit own branch preparation, roadmap traceability, classification, and report assembly
Retains architecture ownership for module, dependency, data, and transaction judgments
Requires a clear roadmap before comparing the implementation
Does not turn the audit into an architecture rewrite
